answer: Each identity tends one ridge beacon that must release a plume whose drift follows the seed's wind, while its dye stains the valley lake a ripple of the same color, read by a seed-chosen neighbor beacon. Lighting it costs a one-time 80 POA calibration fee paid to that neighbor, held three epochs; if plume and ripple disagree, the neighbor keeps the fee and the beacon goes dark four epochs. Ten clones share one operator's dye mix, so their plumes carry identical mineral dust; the lake reader voids all ten at once, 800 POA lost and ten beacons dark, a cost no clone can split or reuse.
